gen-gf-cherry-swash-montserrat: Cherry Swash flares a horseshoe-shaped c and gives its diagonals the same heft as its verticals. But Montserrat is the one that glides, leaving generous white space before every curve.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall, with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e. Beneath Cherry Swash, a full paragraph of it reads smoothly, each stroke cut to a single width with nothing pinching shut.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-switzer: Distinctive from the first glance, Cherry Swash wears a horseshoe c and diagonals weighted like its verticals. Switzer does the quieter work, tubular and wire-like, with a tall waist line and c tips that never touch.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-work-sans: Work Sans sets its mean line high and keeps its c tips well apart, which feels thoroughly modern. Cherry Swash, meanwhile, brings the drama with a horseshoe c, leaving the steady reading to its partner.
gen-gf-comic-relief-archivo: Words read tall and editorial here, curves opening outward instead of curling in, beneath the bold, single-width strokes of Comic Relief. Archivo carries the sentences with its commanding x-height, and Comic Relief saves its voice for loud moments.
gen-gf-comic-relief-fs-asap: Comic Relief draws every letter as if with a marker tip, bowls left open on one side. Asap keeps its body height close to the capitals, so the marker-tip play and the readable text stay clearly apart.
gen-gf-comic-relief-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Comic Relief leaves its bowls unfinished on one side. Be Vietnam Pro sits across from it with strokes like a bent steel rod and curve endings that never crowd each other.
gen-gf-comic-relief-fs-epilogue: Comic Relief makes no visible difference between up and side strokes, and it leaves its bowls unfinished on one side. Epilogue stands tall and wiry beneath it, curvy and unclamped.
gen-gf-comic-relief-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans has a larger-than-usual x-height and s curves that open wide at both ends. Fira Sans stays quiet on the page while Comic Relief, with its unfinished bowls, does the shouting.
gen-gf-comic-relief-fs-merriweather-sans: Bold from the first word, Comic Relief keeps a single-width stroke in every glyph, while Merriweather Sans stands tall and sturdy. Merriweather Sans also lets each e open clearly to the right.
